liam: hi all, liam here  new infra hire. trying to set up access to Vault for a feature branch service. I followed the onboarding doc but `vault kv get secret/data/feature/flag` returns permission denied. What am I missing?

maya: hey @liam — welcome! common misses: 1) you might have a token scoped to `secret/data/dev/*` only, 2) service account not bound to the Vault role, or 3) using AppRole without a proper role-id/secret-id. Which auth method did you use?

liam: using the service account flow (GCP IAM -> Vault auth). I exported VAULT_TOKEN after login with the gcp helper. Token looks short-lived.

forest: quick sanity checks: `vault token lookup` (see ttl/roles) and `vault auth list` to confirm you're on the expected mount. If its the GCP auth method, ensure the IAM principal is mapped in the role: `vault read auth/gcp/role/infra-ci`. The mapping includes the GCP service account email and allowed policies.

liam: ran `vault token lookup` and it shows policies: [dev-read], ttl 1h. The secret path I need is under `secret/data/feature/ci` which requires `feature-read` policy.

maya: yup, request `feature-read` in the access portal. For new hires, use temporary duration (30d) and list the exact paths. Also pick whether you need read-only or write. portal fields: service account, repo, environment, vault paths, KMS key (if envelope), justification.

security-bot: new access request created: AR-7821 by liam. Status: pending triage. Link: https://onboard.redwood.com/AR-7821

liam: thanks. quick follow-up: we use envelope encryption for a few things. if I need to decrypt locally, do I request KMS decrypt or is Vault able to unwrap?

forest: Vault can do transit unwrap if the key is in its transit engine. For envelope patterns where data is encrypted with KMS and stored in Vault, you'll need both: 1) KMS decrypt permission on the key ring (roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter) and 2) Vault policy allowing transit/decrypt or secret read depending on pattern. Ask for both in the portal.

maya: rotation basics: for Vault-managed secrets we use dynamic credentials when possible (DB creds TTLed). For static secrets we set a rotation schedule on the secret engine (e.g., rotate API keys monthly). For KMS keys we rely on GCP key rotation policy; services should not hardcode key versions.

liam: what happens to existing ciphertexts when a KMS key rotates? I guess ciphertexts still decrypt?

forest: GCP KMS uses key versions. ciphertexts include the version used; KMS keeps old versions until you destroy them. Rotation creates a new primary version; old versions remain usable for decrypt until destroyed. So no immediate trouble, but data owners should plan to re-encrypt if they want to retire old versions.

security-bot: AR-7821 approved by eng-security. ACLs will be applied within 20 minutes.

liam: got access, can read secret now. couple of notes for the docs: the portal doesn't make it obvious to select KMS perms separately. Might be worth a tiny UX note.

maya: great feedback  open a doc PR? we can link to it from the onboarding checklist. Also, if youre building a long-running service, we recommend creating a dedicated service account with restricted scope, not using user accounts.

liam: will do, thanks everyone. planning to pair with forest on dynamic DB creds later this week.
